overviewHtml:
Workflows live in one environment, and teams need a way to back them up, promote them to another environment or keep them in version control.

What you get

  • Example curl calls to list, get and create workflows
  • A workflow that commits every workflow definition to a GitHub repository
  • A workflow that creates a workflow from a definition in GitHub
prereqsHtml:
• Dynatrace SaaS with Workflows
  • For the API: an OAuth client with the scopes automation:workflows:read, automation:workflows:write and automation:workflows:run
  • For the GitHub workflows: a GitHub repository and token, and api.github.com in the allowed outbound connections
setupHtml:
API:

  1. Create the OAuth client and get a bearer token.
  2. To browse the API, open the API documentation app from the Launcher and select the Automation definition. You can also download the OpenAPI file there.
  3. Use the calls in api-examples.txt: GET /platform/automation/v1/workflows and GET /platform/automation/v1/workflows/{id} to export, POST /platform/automation/v1/workflows to import.

Workflows:

  1. Import the JSON file through the API (or upload it in Workflows).
  2. Fill in the GitHub details (see Configuration) and run it.
getStartedHtml:
You need Dynatrace Workflows and, for the GitHub workflows, a repository and token.

  1. Create an OAuth client and get a bearer token
  2. Try the example API calls
  3. Import a GitHub workflow and fill in your repository details
